newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat futures rise in nearby months on weather.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat futures rise in nearby months on weather.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures on Tuesday rose in near-term contracts but fell in more distant months in weather-driven moderate trading.
The two nearest contracts both traded higher. May 1997 rose by A$1.00 to A$195.50 a tonne on four lots traded, while July 1997 sold A$5.50 higher to A$198.50 on 16 lots traded.
Settlement prices for contracts covering the September 1997 to September 1998 period all fell, by between 50 cents and A$5.00 a tonne.
Phil Lindsay of Ord Minnett Jardine Fleming Futures said the SFE market was based on domestic issues.
Physical stocks remained tight. Australia's east and west coasts were still dry despite scattered rain which was not enough to alleviate grower concern that a drought might be forming, he said.
This, together with good demand from feed mills, had caused spot months to stay firm.

The scattering of rain, however, had attracted some hedge grower selling in the new crop January 1998 contract at A$180.00 a tonne. Growers were not prepared at present to go down to the bid quote of A$177.50, he said.
The USDA crop report, released overnight, had not influenced the Australian market, he said.

Chicago wheat closed lower overnight on a collapse in soybean futures, after the USDA unexpectedly left soybean stocks unchanged, and on bearishness over a greater than expected USDA forecast for 1996/97 U.S. wheat carryover stocks.
